sources.title: Public Investment in Resource-Abundant Developing Countries
sources.read: Introduction; pp7–8 basket and numeraire equations; pp14–16 calibration discussion and Table1, bounded research reading.
sources.use: Distinct traded/nontraded prices, saving, investment and maintenance. Its substitution and output elasticities are not the basket supply elasticity tested here; no coefficients transferred.

sources.title: On the Capacity to Absorb Public Investment: How Much is Too Much?
sources.read: Abstract, introduction, theoretical framework and data description; institutional summary.
sources.use: Construction unit costs can respond to investment scale and acceleration. Road-project coefficients and GDP thresholds are not lunar calibration.

sources.title: Dutch Disease: Wealth Managed Unwisely
sources.author: Christine Ebrahimzadeh
sources.use: Spending and resource-movement channels are separate. Export proceeds need actual expenditure transactions to affect domestic prices.

sources.title: Frequently asked questions about the Consumer Price Index
sources.read: Index construction, quality adjustment and alternative price measures.
sources.use: Different baskets measure different price changes; domestic final-use index is not a household CPI.

unresolved_retrievals: IMF CPI manual chapter-2 direct PDF URL returned404. That unavailable file supplies no input; ABS methodological guidance supplies the basket distinction.
limits: Targeted primary and institutional reading. The spending shares, basket valuation multipliers and supply elasticities are uncalibrated experiments. No source identifies a lunar inflation rate or converts physical capacity utilization to prices.
